group: TAM / TACO / TMAC — marker and close variants (inventory rows 16, 17, 19, 29, 30, 36, 41; roots BZL CLL HOL RBL / ESX NQX RTX YMX / ESQ NQQ RTQ / BZS CLS / CLC / GCD / HGF)
is_trade_type_variant:
TRADE-TYPE VARIANTS, all seven shapes — and CME says so in its own words, not by inference. But every one of them ALSO carries a published trading window that ends at the marker instant and is NOT the underlying's close, so "variant" does not mean "reuse the underlying's key" here.

(a) They are variants, not products. Energy TAM FAQ: "TAM is a pricing mechanism for a transaction in the applicable underlying futures contract. Fees, positions limits, and reporting levels are based on what applies to the underlying futures contract." Copper TAM FAQ, under the heading "Is a trade in Copper TAM different to a trade in COMEX Copper Futures?": "No, it is not. Copper TAM transaction allows market participants to trade in the COMEX Copper Futures contract at the London Marker Price, plus or minus the transaction price of the TAM trade. Once the London Marker Price is established, Copper TAM trades are resolved into positions in the COMEX Copper Futures contract." TMAC FAQ: "Once the marker price is established, the price of the underlying futures position will be determined by adding the agreed upon spread to the marker price." TACO page: "For all TACO transactions, once the official opening index level is published, the associated futures are cleared at a price equal to the opening cash index level, plus the agreed upon basis." The TMAC/BTIC comparison guide tabulates them under "DELIVERED POSITION (E-MINI FUTURES)": TACO -> ES, NQ, RTY; TMAC -> ES, NQ, RTY, YM.

(b) But the window is genuinely different, and CME publishes it as a window, not merely as a marker instant. This is the specific trap the brief named, so I checked each shape against a CME sentence that states a SESSION boundary rather than an expiry/settlement instant:
- Energy TAM (CLL/BZL/HOL/RBL, CLS/BZS, CLC): "CLS and BZS trading halts at the marker time, daily, at 4:30 p.m. Singapore time (2:30/3:30 a.m. Central time). CLC trading halts at the marker time, daily, at 3:00 p.m. China time (1:00/2:00 a.m. Central time). CLL, RBL, HOL and BZL trading halts at the marker time, daily, at 4:30 p.m. London time." That is CME stating a daily trading halt of the instrument, coincident with the marker. It matches the TradingSessionList closes exactly (15:30Z / 08:30Z / 07:00Z on 2026-08-31 = 16:30 London BST / 16:30 SGT / 15:00 China).
- TMAC (ESX/NQX/RTX/YMX): a published contract-spec row, "TRADING HOURS — CME Globex: Sunday - Friday 6:00 p.m. - 4:00 p.m. ET", against the E-mini underlying's 6:00 p.m. - 5:00 p.m. ET. Matches the feed close 20:00Z = 16:00 ET exactly. I deliberately did NOT use the adjacent "TERMINATION OF TRADING" row on the same page ("TMAC trading shall terminate at 4:00 P.M. ET on the business day immediately preceding the last trade date for such futures contract") — that is contract expiry, the exact confusion that nearly produced six event-contract families.
- TACO (ESQ/NQQ/RTQ): published contract-spec row, "Trading Hours — 10:00 a.m. CT previous day to 8:30 AM CT / For each trade day, trading starts at 10:00 a.m. CT the previous day." Both endpoints match the feed (ready 15:00Z = 10:00 CT on T-1; close 13:30Z = 08:30 CT on T). 08:30 CT is also the 09:30 ET cash open (the marker), but CME states it as the trading-hours end.
- Gold TAM (GCD) and Copper TAM (HGF): I found NO CME sentence stating a session boundary. All I retrieved is the marker calculation window ("Gold futures PM markers are calculated from trade data from 3:00 p.m. – 3:02 p.m. prevailing London time"; copper "12:34 p.m. – 12:35 p.m. London Time") and, for copper, an order-entry cutoff ("may enter any of the following TAM prices up until 12:34:59 p.m. London time"). The feed closes (14:02Z = 15:02 London; 11:35Z = 12:35 London) line up with the marker instants. Under the brief's rule that is precisely the case where a marker instant must not be read as a daily close, so these two stay unresolved.

(c) Consequence for keying: reuse is barred both by evidence and by the repo's own scoping text. `globex_energy` is documented "Excludes TAS/TAM/BTIC, options, and products whose own specification publishes a different grid"; `globex_equity_index` is documented "Excludes full-size S&P 500 (`SP`), Nikkei 225 Dollar (`NKD`), and BTIC/TACO products". Mapping any of these roots to those keys would report the wrong close by 5.5 hours (TAM London), 12.5 hours (TAM Singapore), 1 hour (TMAC) or 7.5 hours (TACO).

This is the best-evidenced shape in the group: CME publishes a complete current window that matches the feed byte for byte — "TRADING HOURS — CME Globex: Sunday - Friday 6:00 p.m. - 4:00 p.m. ET" (feed: Ready 22:00Z = 17:00 CT = 18:00 ET, Close 20:00Z = 15:00 CT = 16:00 ET). roots_unresolved: GCD (row 36, gold TAM, group 78:GM) — cannot determine whether the 14:02Z close is a session boundary. What IS sourced: the product exists and its listing is dated — CME Clearing advisory #17-356, notice date 15 September 2017, effective date 23 October 2017, "Initial listing of TAM based on the Gold PM marker price for trading on CME Globex and for submission for clearing through CME ClearPort" — and the marker window is sourced: "Gold futures PM markers are calculated from trade data from 3:00 p.m. – 3:02 p.m. prevailing London time." The feed's daily Close at 14:02Z = 15:02 London BST is exactly the end of that marker window. What is NOT sourced: any CME statement that GCD trading halts or closes at that instant. The energy TAM FAQ's explicit "trading halts at the marker time, daily" sentence names only CLS/BZS/CLC/CLL/RBL/HOL — it does not cover metals. Asserting a 15:02 London daily close for GCD on the schedule file alone would be reading a marker instant as a session close, which is the failure mode the brief flagged. Also unresolved: GCD is only one of three published gold markers (AM London 10:30–10:32, PM London 3:00–3:02, Asia 3:25–3:30 China time), so any gold-TAM key must be scoped to the PM marker and must not silently absorb the AM or Asia marker roots. Leave GCD unmapped until a CME trading-hours or session statement for it is retrieved.

HGF (row 41, copper TAM, April group 78:TR) — cannot determine, and the joined row may additionally be stale. What IS sourced: the marker, twice. The COMEX Copper TAM FAQ tabulates "Copper TAM Marker Name / TAM Code / Calculation Period — Copper London Marker | HGF | 12:34 p.m. - 12:35 p.m. London Time" and states "The Marker Price ... called the 'COMEX Copper London Marker price'. It is published every business day at 12:35 p.m. London time"; the metals-markers page repeats "Trade data from 12:34 p.m. – 12:35 p.m. London Time". The feed's Close at 11:35Z = 12:35 London BST matches. The nearest thing to a session statement is an ORDER-ENTRY cutoff, not a session close: "A trader seeking to lock in Copper TAM price before it has been determined may enter any of the following TAM prices up until 12:34:59 p.m. London time." That is suggestive but is not CME saying the instrument's trading session ends there, so I will not assert a close from it. TWO FURTHER PROBLEMS. (1) INVENTORY LABEL IS WRONG: row 41 is titled "copper TAM 12:00", but the exact transitions for signature e9c75914...48cc are 336=4 at 11:35:00Z daily, i.e. 12:35 London / 06:35 CT — not 12:00 of any zone. The "12:00" appears to have been carried over from row 18 (copper TAS, 13:00 ET = 12:00 CT). Anyone sizing this work from the inventory label alone will model the wrong hour. (2) ROUTE DRIFT: the audit itself records "HGF 78/TR -> 78/HT" between the April definition key and the 2026-08-28 product sheet, so the August 78:TR row (described "TAM COPPER (HGF)") may no longer be HGF's group. The envelope must be re-derived from a schedule week that is time-aligned with the root before any table is written. Leave HGF unmapped.
